title: Add modular authoring-studio playbook and sandboxed tool-factory docs
author: Sofia Nguyen
release_notes: Adds a modular authoring-studio playbook and a sandboxed tool-factory quickstart for RAG workflows; non-breaking docs-only PR.
description: Context: Teams building retrieval-augmented generation pipelines asked for a concise, modular playbook that shows iterative authoring patterns, versioned prompt sets, and a lightweight 'tool-factory' sandbox for creating and testing tool-call stubs locally without spinning up full backend services. Motivation: reduce onboarding friction for product and infra engineers by providing a single-playbook flow that demonstrates best practices for incremental indexing, structured output checks, telemetry probes, and safe tool-calling patterns. What this PR changes: 1) Adds a modular playbook page that walks through stages: project bootstrap, index strategy, prompt families and canary evaluations, stepwise debugging with replayable traces, and rollout guidance for canary->gradual->global; 2) Adds a sandboxed tool-factory guide and sample stubs in TypeScript that run as an in-process mock server and a CLI to bind tools to an agent persona; 3) Adds diagrams and an SVG flow that can be embedded in the docs site; 4) Adds a small quickstart script that creates a seeded local index, runs the agent against a canned dataset, and emits structured evaluation artifacts for comparison. Implementation notes: This is docs-only with code samples under docs/authoring-studio/examples and a tiny shell helper under docs/snippets; samples are intentionally small and non-production to avoid accidental reuse as operational code. The playbook emphasizes incremental evaluation: seed->simulate->assert->rollout. Checklist: - [x] Playbook draft written and reviewed by product - [x] Tool-factory sample implements two example tools (search-stub, calculator-stub) and includes interface docs - [x] Quickstart script tested locally on macOS and Linux WSL - [x] Accessibility pass on new diagrams - [x] CI docs lint passing Commits: 4 commits: initial playbook scaffold and outline; add tool-factory TypeScript stubs and README; add quickstart script, diagrams and examples; docs polish and typo fixes. Files changed: docs/authoring-studio/playbook.md, docs/authoring-studio/tool-factory.md, docs/authoring-studio/images/authoring-flow.svg, docs/authoring-studio/examples/ts-tool-factory-stub.ts, docs/snippets/seed-quickstart.sh, site/sidebar.yml. CI and checks: docs-lint succeeded, spellcheck reported two false positives that were acknowledged, link-checker passed for internal links but flagged an external CDN which was whitelisted. Review summary: Priya requested a small clarifying callout about telemetry privacy which was added to the playbook and linked to the security runbook; Ethan asked for a more explicit error-handling example in the tool stub which was added in the second commit; Liam requested an inline example showing how to convert a legacy embedding pipeline to the playbook's incremental index, added as a short code snippet. Approvals: All three reviewers approved after the second iteration. Merge details: Squash-merged to main after CI green and a manual visual check of the diagrams in staging. Migration notes and follow-ups: - Add a short video walkthrough to the docs site in a follow-up PR (PM-452). - Proposal to add a runnable workshop that provisions a temporary Dedicated sandbox for paid users (ENG-1378). - Consider converting the TypeScript stubs into an official quickstart repo if uptake is high. Links: internal playbook prototype doc: https://linear.app/PROJECT/board/ENG-1378 and related spec in the product brief PM-452. This PR is intentionally conservative: examples are sandboxed and non-networked by default to avoid exposing credentials or running services in CI.
commits_summary: 4 commits: scaffold playbook; add tool-factory TS examples and README; add quickstart script and diagrams; docs polish and fixes

Liam: Include migration snippet from legacy embedding pipeline; added snippet. Author: addressed all comments, added unit test for quickstart, pushed fixes. Reviewers approved on 2025-09-19.
